sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 1990 BMW 320is Coupe, finished in Delphin Grey Metallic with a grey and black interior. This 320is features a dogleg 5-speed manual transmission. This BMW is a foreign-market coupe. Its odometer reads in metric units and currently indicates approximately 220,300 kilometers, or roughly 136,900 miles. A partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes the M-Technic II appearance kit, a limited-slip differential, a sunroof, cloth upholstery, front sport seats, and power-operated windows. Notable modifications reported by the seller include 15-inch Ronal wheels, a Supersprint mid-section exhaust, Bilstein B6 shock absorbers, aftermarket front control arm bushings, and an Alpine AM/FM/cassette head unit. BMW's iconic E30 revolutionized the compact luxury sports segment with a varied model range that included sedans, coupes, wagons, convertibles, and performance-oriented models. Today, the E30 is highly sought-after by enthusiasts who value the analog driving experience and instantly recognizable styling of an early 3 Series. Commonly known as the "Italian M3", the E30 320is was marketed in Europe as a displacement-based tax-break alternative to the full-blooded M3. Featuring a de-stroked, 2.0-liter version of the Ur-M3's 2.3-liter, race-bred S14 twin-cam four, it was even keener to rev to its 7,200 rpm redline. Commonly quoted production figures show that fewer than 4,000 coupe and sedan versions were built over a three year run. Power comes from an S14B20 2.0-liter 4-cylinder, rated at about 192 horsepower and 155 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels through a 5-speed manual transmission.
